t: Crown rule replaced the East India Company in 1858, after the rebellion of 1857, and lasted until independence in 1947.
A viceroy ruled British provinces directly and more than 560 princely states indirectly, with the Indian Civil Service at its core.
Gandhi’s mass campaigns and the Second World War ended British rule, and partition into India and Pakistan cost hundreds of thousands of lives.
dyk: The Indian Army of the Second World War, about 2.5 million strong, is often described as the largest all-volunteer army in history.
ev: The Government of India Act transfers the East India Company’s territories to the Crown
Queen Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar
The Indian National Congress is founded in Bombay
George V announces the move of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
Troops kill hundreds of unarmed people at the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar
Gandhi leads the Salt March to Dandi
Congress launches the Quit India movement
Independence and partition create India and Pakistan on 14–15 August

f.capital: Calcutta; later New Delhi (from 1911/1931); Simla in summer
f.founder: British Crown (Government of India Act 1858); first viceroy Lord Canning
f.successor: Dominion of India; Dominion of Pakistan
